key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial agent substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The study points to a scalable, more sustainable pathway for carbon capture and conversion by pairing catalyst design with a carbon-negative biological scavenger.
method: Leveraged layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy to improve charge transport and separation
Used microalgae during photocatalysis and compared performance against no scavenger and microplastics
evidence_signal: Compared with HEO-only catalysis, adding microalgae increased CO production about 10-fold and CH4 production about 4-fold, outperforming systems with or without microplastics.
watch_item: The abstract does not report long-term stability, reactor scalability, or the practical logistics of integrating living microalgae with photocatalytic operation.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
